articles.t: GTA 6 : une fuite révèle ce que la PS5 Pro pousserait plus loin que les autres consoles
articles.chapeau: Une liste attribuée à Tex2 compare GTA 6 sur consoles. Ombres, textures, population : les différences rapportées et les améliorations déjà confirmées.
articles.txt:
Visuel d’illustration repris de Sumahodigest ; représentation conceptuelle, apparence non officielle.
La PS5 Pro ne pousserait pas tous les réglages de GTA 6 au maximum. Une liste attribuée au dataminer du compte @TexFunz2, suggère plutôt une base proche de celle de la PS5 et de la Xbox Series X, renforcée sur l’éclairage et les ombres en ray tracing. La Xbox Series S utiliserait de son côté des paramètres plus modestes sur plusieurs aspects du monde. Ce relevé non officiel donne une lecture intéressante des compromis entre consoles.
Le document a été détaillé le 25 novembre par MP1st , qui renvoie vers une publication du compte @TexFunz2 . Les valeurs sont présentées comme issues des données du jeu : il ne s’agit ni d’un menu de réglages destiné aux joueurs, ni d’un comparatif de performances réalisé par Menow. Leur portée doit donc rester celle d’une fuite technique.
La fuite place l’illumination globale sur un niveau élevé pour la PS5 Pro, contre moyen pour les autres consoles. Elle décrit aussi des ombres directionnelles et locales en ray tracing activées sur la Pro. Cette dernière se distinguerait ainsi par la manière de calculer la lumière et les ombres, plutôt que par une hausse uniforme de chaque curseur.
Le point général rejoint une amélioration déjà officielle. Dans sa présentation des fonctionnalités de GTA VI sur PlayStation , Sony indiquait que la PS5 Pro apporte des ombres en ray tracing et une meilleure netteté grâce au PSSR, la reconstruction d’image propre à la console. L’annonce commerciale confirme ces fonctions, sans authentifier pour autant chaque valeur du tableau qui circule.
Ces deux techniques ne font pas le même travail. Les ombres en ray tracing touchent au calcul de l’éclairage ; le PSSR sert à reconstruire une image plus détaillée à partir du rendu. Leur combinaison peut améliorer la présentation visuelle, mais ne se résume pas à une simple augmentation de la résolution. Les différences peuvent aussi varier suivant les lieux et les conditions d’éclairage d’une scène.
Ces niveaux traduits servent à comprendre la liste divulguée. Ils ne constituent pas des intitulés français vérifiés dans un menu de GTA 6.
La reprise de Sumahodigest souligne la proximité entre PS5 et Xbox Series X : textures, cheveux, simulation de l’eau ou densité du trafic sont notamment présentés comme communs. Cela suggère une même orientation de qualité pour ces éléments, plutôt que deux versions radicalement différentes du monde.
Il faut toutefois distinguer un niveau de paramètre et son résultat complet à l’écran. Une étiquette « élevée » ne renseigne pas à elle seule sur la résolution interne, la reconstruction de l’image, la stabilité temporelle ou les baisses de fluidité pendant une scène chargée. Le tableau ne suffit donc pas à départager définitivement deux consoles.
Pour le joueur, la comparaison utile se situe dans une situation équivalente : même lieu, même éclairage, mouvements proches et séquence suffisamment longue pour observer les variations. Un arrêt sur image révèle certains détails ; un déplacement peut en montrer d’autres, notamment la stabilité des contours ou l’apparition des éléments lointains. Cette méthode permet de relier les réglages supposés à des différences réellement visibles.
Les informations relayées mentionnent, sur Series S, une baisse de qualité pour plusieurs catégories : végétation, particules, cheveux, simulation ou densité du monde. La réduction supposée ne concernerait donc pas uniquement la finesse d’une surface regardée de près. Elle pourrait aussi se manifester dans la richesse d’une scène ou dans le nombre d’éléments simultanément présents.
Cela ne permet pas de déduire que des missions ou des quartiers disparaissent. Les paramètres d’affichage et de simulation décrits ne constituent pas une liste de contenus. Le degré exact de différence doit être apprécié dans le jeu ; il serait trompeur de présenter un niveau interne comme une mesure directe de l’expérience entière.
La question d’un mode plus fluide revient naturellement dès qu’une version réserve une partie de sa puissance aux effets visuels. La liste divulguée n’établit pourtant ni l’existence d’un mode sans ray tracing accessible aux joueurs, ni le nombre d’images par seconde qu’il atteindrait. Une hypothèse d’allègement graphique reste différente d’une fonctionnalité programmée et testée.
Dans sa présentation technique de la PS5 Pro , Sony décrit un GPU renforcé, davantage de ressources pour le ray tracing et le PSSR.

articles.chapeau: Take-Two used a DMCA notice to remove Leonida, the GTA 6 PC port project, covering 1 repo and 2,900+ forks. What is confirmed and what is not.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. has shut down Leonida, an unofficial project that aimed to bring Grand Theft Auto VI to PC. The company, which owns Rockstar Games, sent GitHub a DMCA takedown request covering one repository and more than 2,900 forks, and GitHub removed the project after the complaint. Reports from Mashable, The Verge, Eurogamer, Nacionale, Metro.co.uk and NoobFeed, dated between November 24 and 26, 2026, describe the sequence.
This analysis takes a different angle than our first-day report on the Leonida DMCA action . Instead of retelling the headline, it asks what the notice says, why the fork count matters, how a takedown against a fork network works in general terms, and what PC players and developers should take from it. It also flags every claim that remains unconfirmed, because the rumor mill around this game has been loud all month.
The short version has three anchors. Take-Two says Leonida infringed its copyrighted works. No PC release date for GTA 6 has been confirmed. And nothing in the confirmed record shows the project produced a complete, playable PC port. Everything below builds on those three points.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Start with what the record supports. The project was called Leonida. Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., the parent company of Rockstar Games, submitted a DMCA takedown request to GitHub. The request named ItsNotRexed’s GitHub repository and more than 2,900 forks attached to it. GitHub then removed the project following the complaint.
The project was described in coverage as an unofficial effort to run or bring Grand Theft Auto VI to PC. That wording matters. Reports describe an attempt, not a finished product. Nothing in the confirmed facts says a player could download Leonida and boot a stable game, and several outlets stopped short of claiming that.
Reports dated November 24 through 26, 2026 describe the takedown, which makes this a story that broke across a single news cycle. It moved fast because the game itself dominates gaming search right now, and PC players have spent weeks hunting for any sign of a port. A takedown against the most visible fan attempt answers one question and raises several others.
The notice identified its sender as the IP Enforcement Team for Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., parent company of Rockstar Games. That phrasing is worth a second look. The request came from the corporate parent’s enforcement group, not from a studio spokesperson, which tells you this is a routine legal workflow rather than a public relations gesture. Large publishers keep dedicated teams for this work, and notices like this one tend to go out quietly and in volume.
The core statement is short. Take-Two wrote: “We are writing to submit a takedown request regarding ItsNotRexed’s GitHub repository and the 2900+ forks attached to it that infringes upon Take-Two’s copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI.”
Read it closely and two separate theories appear. The first says the repository itself infringes Take-Two’s copyrighted works. The second says it facilitates infringement of Grand Theft Auto VI by others. A rights holder can lean on either theory, and pairing them makes the notice harder to dodge on a technicality. Take-Two did not need to prove that Leonida distributed the game. It only needed to assert that the project helped others copy it.
A single repository is easy to remove. A fork network is the real enforcement problem. On GitHub, anyone can copy a public repository into their own account with one click, and each copy carries the full code and history. When a project goes viral, those copies multiply within hours, which is exactly the dynamic that makes a 2,900-plus fork count so telling.
By naming the forks in the same notice, Take-Two avoided a slow game of whack-a-mole. Filing separate complaints against thousands of accounts would take weeks. A single notice that references the repository and its attached forks compresses that work into one step. For a publisher with a high-value launch to protect, the economics are obvious.

articles.chapeau: Cyberleek released the main executable for its leaked 209GB GTA 6 Xbox build on 23 November, and the open source VIctory project says the game boots on Windows but runs at about 1 frame per second in the world, not playable.
articles.txt:
Practical fixes for the tech you already own. Free, a few times a week.
The main executable for the leaked Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto 6 began circulating on 23 November 2026, according to TalkEsport . XDA Developers reported that the executable had become public and completed the Xbox build. Cyberleek put the size of the rest of that build at around 209GB, according to TalkEsport. The open source project VIctory says in its GitHub README that the game boots on a Windows PC and reaches the prologue. The project reports about 1 frame per second in the game world and describes the game as unplayable at that frame rate.
PC Gamer reported that Cyberleek had released a near-complete Xbox build the previous week but had held back the main executable. Cyberleek had said it would release the file when its crypto coin reached a $15 million market cap or on 23 November, whichever came first. TalkEsport reported that the rest of the build had been online since 19 November. According to accounts tracking the release, which TalkEsport cited, the executable began circulating shortly before 3pm UTC on 23 November.
Cyberleek called the release “an early Christmas gift” for followers, according to PC Gamer. The outlet reported that Cyberleek framed the release as a handover to people trying to get the game running on PC. Cyberleek added, “The torch passes to the open source recomp and emulation projects.” PC Gamer’s Andy Chalk wrote that Cyberleek appeared to have followed through on the release and said he had not verified whether the executable was genuine.
XDA identified Cyberleek as the same individual or group behind GTA 6 leaks from earlier in the year. It also reported that Cyberleek had published SHA-256 hashes for both the executable and its ZIP archive. XDA’s report appeared on 23 November, the day the executable began circulating, and the outlet updated it on 24 November.
TalkEsport reported that clips showed the leaked build reaching its opening settings screens on PC within hours of the executable’s release. TalkEsport said none of the progress it covered had been independently verified.
VIctory’s GitHub repository was created at 21:47 UTC on 23 November 2026, according to GitHub’s records. The project uses the GPL-3.0 license. The repository was created the same day the executable began circulating, according to the dates reported by GitHub and TalkEsport. In a status update dated 25 November 2026, the README says the title boots, the menus run at 30 fps and the game loads its world. The README also says it plays the intro cutscene and reaches the prologue.
The menus and the world run at different speeds in VIctory’s account. The README says, “Not playable yet, because of the framerate: about 1 frame per second in the world.” The project reports testing on one machine running Windows 11 and equipped with an AMD RX 6700 XT graphics card with 12 GB of memory. The frame rates and milestones in the README describe that test. The README names the frame rate as what keeps the game from being playable. It also warns that entering the world hung the GPU in earlier builds and that a run can still end on a GPU fault.
XDA’s 24 November update named VIctory among the unofficial GTA 6 PC projects tracked by a site called PortWatch VI, and said that site probably isn’t an entirely accurate picture of the projects’ status. The same update reported, according to Leonida developer NotRexed, that the Leonida project was removed from GitHub after a DMCA notice .
PC Gamer warned that files from strangers can contain malware. TalkEsport reported that security firms were warning about fake GTA 6 PC downloads spreading malware. Make Tech Easier reported that a GTA 6 PC port scam kit was being offered on the dark web for $200 in Bitcoin or Tether, citing NordVPN.
As of TalkEsport’s report, Rockstar Games had yet to announce a PC version of GTA 6. The outlet reported that neither Rockstar Games nor Take-Two Interactive had made a public comment about the leak. VIctory’s README says the game reached the prologue in its Windows test. The project’s account says the game was unplayable because of the frame rate once it loaded the world.

articles.t: GTA 6 PC Leak: 1 Xbox Build, 0 Official PC Dates
articles.chapeau: A leaked Xbox build of GTA 6 has PC gamers hopeful, but Rockstar has announced no GTA 6 PC version, date or specs. Here is the catch.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games A new GTA 6 leak is handing PC gamers something they have wanted since Rockstar Games shipped Grand Theft Auto VI on consoles: a possible way in. The catch is big. Rockstar has not announced a PC version, and Grand Theft Auto VI is not officially available on PC, according to Polygon’s coverage of the story.
The leaker known as Cyberleek reportedly released an executable tied to a leaked Xbox build of the game, described as a November 2026 build. Our earlier report on the 57 MB executable leak covered the first wave of that drop and found no playable PC build. This analysis looks at what the leak means, what it does not prove, and where the hype is running ahead of the evidence.
The list of confirmed facts is short, so we keep it separate from the rumor pile. Anything not on that list gets labeled as unconfirmed, attributed to reports, or left out. If you came here for a PC release date, a price, or a spec sheet, the honest answer today is that none of them exist officially.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Reports say Cyberleek released an executable associated with a leaked Xbox build of Grand Theft Auto VI. The build is described as dating from November 2026. Cyberleek reportedly wrote that “CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent.”
That one sentence is the only on-record statement from the leaker in the reporting we reviewed. It claims possession of a full build and says distribution happens by torrent. It does not say the build runs on a PC, and it does not say the files are complete in any way a normal player could use.
The game itself is developed by Rockstar Games and goes by both Grand Theft Auto VI and GTA 6. Both names show up in the coverage, and both refer to the same title. The Xbox label matters because the leaked build targets Microsoft’s console, not a PC storefront or a PlayStation release.
Polygon framed the episode around a simple tension. The leak looks like good news for people waiting on a GTA 6 PC release, yet it comes with a catch that the headline itself flags. We unpack both halves below, starting with why PC players care.
PC players have spent months watching console owners play. A leak involving an Xbox build feeds a hope that PC is a short technical step away. That hope is understandable. It is also, for now, a feeling rather than a finding.
In our analysis, the Xbox angle explains much of the excitement. Xbox consoles run on x86 processors and a graphics stack that sits close to what Windows PCs use. Enthusiasts have long watched Xbox builds for that reason, because they tend to be the nearest console relative of a PC version. That closeness is a reason for curiosity, not proof that a leaked build converts cleanly.
The second source of optimism is timing. A build dated November 2026 is recent, which suggests the files reflect the game close to its current state. Still, a recent date says nothing about whether the files are complete, stable, or runnable outside Microsoft’s hardware.
Some fans hope the leak will push Rockstar to move up an official PC release. That hope is on the unconfirmed list. Nothing in the reporting shows Rockstar changing any plan in response, and a company the size of Take-Two does not usually reshuffle a launch schedule because of a leak.
So the good news is narrow. The leak shows a build exists in the wild, and it gives PC gamers a fresh reason to ask Rockstar for a plan. That is all the evidence supports.
Rockstar Games has not officially announced a PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI. Polygon and other outlets in the coverage agree on that point, and it anchors everything else. No release date, price, system requirements, performance targets, or official Rockstar statement on PC exists in the verified reporting.
The gap is not new. Our look at the March 2027 PC talk tracked a single leak with zero Rockstar confirmations. The pattern has repeated since: a claim surfaces, forums amplify it, and the publisher says nothing.
The reporting is blunt here. There is no official statement from Rockstar Games on PC availability in connection with this leak. Silence is not denial, and it is not a green light either. It means readers should treat every PC date and every PC spec in circulation as rumor.

articles.t: GTA 6 After Launch: How Rockstar Keeps the Hype
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 after launch: Rockstar confirmed $79.99 and $99.99 editions plus a 34-track album, but no roadmap. Here is what is known and what is not.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games Grand Theft Auto VI has been on sale for a week, and the conversation has already shifted from when it ships to what happens next. According to Creative Bloq , the real test of the game’s success is not the launch itself. The outlet’s framing is simple: now that the game is out, how does Rockstar keep up the hype? That question matters more than any opening-week headline, because a release date only sets the starting line for a long commercial race.
The facts on the table are narrow. Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc. (NASDAQ: TTWO) announced that Grand Theft Auto VI became available on November 19, 2026, on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar Games said the game “is now available.” Beyond that, Rockstar has not detailed a post-launch roadmap, and our earlier launch coverage already flagged that PC remains undated. This analysis separates what the companies have confirmed from what observers expect, and it labels every forecast as opinion.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
A launch is an event. Success is a trend line. Publishers have understood that gap for years, yet it hits hardest with a title as large as Grand Theft Auto VI, where the marketing machine ran for a long stretch before release day. When a campaign peaks on the day of release, the next phase has to replace it with something that keeps players talking, buying and returning.
Creative Bloq’s argument rests on that logic. A record-sized opening can look impressive on a slide, but it says little about whether players stay engaged a month later, whether word of mouth stays positive, or whether new buyers arrive after the first wave of fans has finished. Those later signals decide how a game gets remembered. They also decide how much value Take-Two extracts from a single release over its life.
The timing adds pressure. The game reached stores on November 19, 2026, which puts it in the middle of the holiday shopping season. That gives Rockstar a built-in second wave of attention as gift buyers enter the market. It also means the studio competes for time and wallet share with every other holiday release, a factor we return to in the competitive section below.
Because the story invites speculation, it helps to pin down the verified record first. Take-Two’s announcement and related Rockstar materials establish a short list of facts. Grand Theft Auto VI launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The standard edition costs $79.99. The Ultimate Edition costs $99.99. The ESRB rated the game M for Mature. The game is a single-player experience.
Distribution details are also on the record. Digital pre-orders could begin pre-loading on November 12, 2026. The physical version, which includes a download code inside the box, also became available on November 12, 2026. A separate product, Grand Theft Auto VI: The Album, carries 34 original tracks and is described as the official soundtrack from Atlantic Records.
Everything outside that table counts as unconfirmed for this article. That includes any content roadmap, any live-service plan, any multiplayer feature, and any specific method Rockstar will use to sustain interest. The company has said none of it in the sources available to us.
Creative Bloq, a design and creative-industry publication, put the idea in its headline: the measure of the game’s success will not be the launch. The framing treats the release as a milestone rather than a verdict. For a publication focused on creative work, that makes sense. Visual identity, trailers, key art and social campaigns drive attention before release, while the product itself has to carry attention afterward.
We cannot reproduce the full text of that piece here, and we do not claim to know every argument inside it. What we can say is that the headline’s thesis is an editorial position, not a measured result. Treat it as informed commentary. No sales ceiling, retention rate or review aggregate in the fact sheet proves or disproves it.
The thesis still holds up on its logic. A marketing push builds anticipation, and anticipation is a finite resource. After release, the audience splits into players who love the game and talk about it, players who finish it and move on, and buyers who wait for a discount. Each group needs a different reason to keep the title in the conversation. Rockstar’s job over the coming months is to serve all

articles.t: The state of GTA 6 on PC: Everything you need to know
articles.chapeau: The race to play GTA 6 on PC is moving by the hour, so here is where every fan port, project, and emulation attempt stands right now.
articles.txt:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is undoubtedly the biggest game ever created, and some might argue it's the biggest entertainment project of all time. Rockstar has confirmed that GTA 6 made $3.79 billion on the first day of launch, shattering entertainment records. It was the most pre-ordered title on both the PlayStation and Xbox stores, and it even earned a spectacular Metacritic score of 99. However, one thing was missing from GTA 6's historic launch.
Rockstar's masterpiece launched on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, but not on PC. That wasn't a surprise omission, but it's still a big chunk of the player base that missed out on experiencing GTA 6 at the same time as the rest of the world. We have come to expect this pattern from Rockstar, as GTA 5 and Red Dead Redemption 2 both launched on PC some time after their original console launches. Most likely, that is exactly what will happen with GTA 6. However, it looks like PC players aren't waiting around.
Popular Now: Rockstar is handing out 100 of these gorgeous limited-edition GTA 6 PS5 consoles, and you can't buy one What Rockstar has said so far First, we have to talk about what Rockstar has officially said. Surprisingly, Rockstar hasn't confirmed a PC version yet, and neither has Take-Two, its parent company. However, given the history of previous Rockstar launches, we can make an educated guess that an official PC version will eventually come out. The closest thing to a timeline is a GamesBeat report in which four industry sources said Rockstar is targeting the first quarter of 2027 for GTA 6 on PC. That was in October, and we haven't heard any new rumors since.
6 A car meet in Grand Theft Auto VI, which launched on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S without a confirmed PC version. VIEW GALLERY - 6 IMAGES Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick said in November that Take-Two is beefing up its defenses against AI-assisted reverse engineering and unofficial PC ports, so they were definitely prepared for the onslaught. Shortly after GTA 6's November 19 launch, people started testing the waters, trying to port GTA 6 to PC themselves. Of course, nobody had any luck at first, but the breakthrough came via notorious leaker Cyberleek, who had been pestering Rockstar for months before launch.
On November 19, Cyberleek announced it had a full November 2026 Xbox build. The roughly 209 GB package was uploaded shortly after, but without the main executable. That part was locked behind a countdown, partly tied to a meme coin goal. Regardless of that attempt to pump up his meme coin, Cyberleek dropped the .exe on November 23, alongside a statement calling the whole thing a protest against subscriptions. At this point, it is important to remember this wasn't a PC build, but an Xbox Series X one. Getting the files and the executable did not mean you could just copy them to your PC, run the .exe, and jump into Leonida. It's not quite that simple.

articles.txt:
Homebrew enthusiasts and piracy groups are eyeing another way to play Rockstar ’s new title. A game dump of the GTA 6 PS5 version is reportedly running via a console jailbreak . While the hack is only compatible with older firmware, it could also make the crime adventure bootable in a PC-based emulator .
Before the GTA 6 release date , reports emerged of a game dump accomplished on firmware 14.22 . Unfortunately, the popular Relapse kernel exploit only works up to 13.60. Some homebrew fans choose to wait, denying themselves the retail Rockstar build. It appears that their patience has paid off.
On November 25th, multiple videos surfaced of the alleged game dump running on a PS5 jailbreak. One clip depicted a car driving through dark Leonida streets. Other footage showed the title installed on the console’s dashboard and the debug menu , identifying firmware 11.60.
ⓘ screenshot, DaniCorpHQ X account (French, translated) Update on GTA 6 game dump and PS5 jailbreak shown Redditors have since verified that the leaked files are being shared on piracy networks. The massive 540 GB download contains the decrypted eboot.bin, which is similar to an .exe file . It also includes the vital sce_sys PlayStation system information folder and assets.
It’s unclear how hackers managed to boot GTA 6 on firmware 11.60, when the retail version requires 14.23. It’s also not yet confirmed whether it’s an option for PS5 jailbreaks with software update 13.60. Regardless, it’s another troubling development for Take-Two Interactive and Rockstar.
Recently, Cyberleek returned and distributed a full Xbox build. Because consoles and PCs share the x86-64 CPU architecture, individuals immediately began adapting the files for Windows. The game is already partially playable , though framerates are seriously compromised. This progress prompted Take-Two to shut down Discord servers and issue DMCA takedowns for GitHub repositories .
The GTA 6 PS5 game dump on a jailbroken PlayStation could also bring the Rockstar project to PCs. One potential solution is the KytyPS5 emulator , available on Windows and Linux. The program supports folder structures with eboot.bin files, like those now spreading on piracy sites. Nevertheless, considerable work remains to stream assets correctly and achieve acceptable performance.

articles.t: GTA 6 à 120 FPS sur PS6 et Xbox Helix, un insider dévoile ses estimations
articles.chapeau: Bloqué à 30 FPS sur PS5 et Xbox Series, GTA 6 rallume pourtant le débat performance avec une fuite ciblant la future PS6 et la Xbox Project Helix. Jusqu’où ces consoles next gen pourraient pousser le compteur d’images par seconde ?
articles.txt:
Bloqué à 30 FPS sur PS5 et Xbox Series, GTA 6 rallume pourtant le débat performance avec une fuite ciblant la future PS6 et la Xbox Project Helix. Jusqu’où ces consoles next gen pourraient pousser le compteur d’images par seconde ?
Pour l’instant, les joueurs consoles vivent GTA 6 en 30 FPS fixes, que ce soit sur PS5 , PS5 Pro ou Xbox Series X|S . Aucun mode 40 ou 60 FPS n’est proposé, Rockstar Games assumant ce choix pour préserver la densité de l’open world et les effets de ray tracing.
Une nouvelle fuite relance pourtant l’espoir des amateurs de fluidité. Le leaker Moore’s Law Is Dead affirme que GTA 6 pourrait tourner en 60 FPS, voire viser un mode 120 FPS, sur la future PlayStation 6 et la Xbox Project Helix . De quoi faire rêver ceux qui jouent déjà sur des téléviseurs 120 Hz.
Sur les machines actuelles, les analyses de Digital Foundry parlent d’un rendu autour du 1440p à 30 FPS sur PS5 et Xbox Series X , avec un avantage pour Xbox grâce au 120 Hz et au VRR. Un bug Quick Resume sur Xbox peut même pousser temporairement GTA 6 au delà de 40 FPS, mais en accélérant le jeu, ce qui le rend injouable.
C’est dans ce contexte que Moore’s Law Is Dead affirme que PS6 et Xbox Helix auront un GPU au niveau d’une GeForce RTX 5080 : dans sa vidéo, il parle d’« the equivalent of a 5080 for the GPU », citation rapportée par Notebookcheck. Selon lui, un 60 FPS stable serait réaliste, avec un mode 120 FPS pensé comme option performance, même si l’insider Kepler_L2 reste nettement plus prudent sur la PS6 .
D’après ces fuites , la PlayStation 6 viserait jusqu’à 40 Compute Units RDNA 5 . Moore’s Law Is Dead va jusqu’à dire que ce GPU pourrait dépasser une RTX 5080 en ray tracing et se rapprocher d’une Radeon RX 9070 XT en rasterisation, ce qui placerait une version next gen de GTA 6 bien au delà des consoles actuelles.
La Xbox Project Helix irait plus loin encore avec jusqu’à 56 Compute Units RDNA 5 , davantage de bande passante mémoire et un recours massif au FSR pour reconstruire une image 4K. Côté processeur, Helix passerait de 8 cœurs Zen 2 à jusqu’à 11 cœurs Zen 6 au delà de 4 GHz, de quoi gommer le goulot d’étranglement CPU qui empêche déjà aujourd’hui GTA 6 de grimper au dessus des 30 FPS.
Moore’s Law Is Dead évoque une mise en production de la PS6 au deuxième trimestre 2027, pour une sortie entre fin 2027 et début 2028. Xbox Helix viserait la même fenêtre , mais avec un positionnement bien plus haut de gamme, autour de 1 000 à 1 200 dollars, soit environ 950 à 1 150 € en Europe.
Dans ce scénario, un Grand Theft Auto VI « Enhanced » pour PS6 et Xbox Helix avec un mode 60 FPS paraît très probable, tandis qu’un mode 120 FPS resterait conditionné à des compromis sur la résolution et le ray tracing. Tant que Rockstar Games ne confirme rien, ces chiffres doivent être vus comme des objectifs ambitieux plutôt que comme une promesse ferme.

articles.t: New 'GTA 6' Leak Is Great News For PC Gamers, But There's A Catch
articles.chapeau: A new leak gives PC players a sense of what to expect from GTA 6 with souped-up settings that aren't possible on PS5 Pro or Xbox
articles.txt:
Much has been said about the differences between Grand Theft Auto 6 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox , but how will Rockstar Games' open-world game fare on PC? An official port has yet to be announced, but a recent leak of the Xbox build of the game has kicked off a race to recompile the game and make it unofficially available on more platforms. As that work continues, yet another leak offers PC players some perspective on what might be possible in GTA 6 when the game isn't held down by console constraints.
On Wednesday, known GTA leaker Tex2 shared a Pastebin that lists GTA 6 's apparent console settings shipped by Rockstar. These are tunable options that exist to help the game shine on platforms with varying capacities, like the less-powerful Xbox Series S. The text dump has since been pulled by Pastebin, but Polygon viewed the document before the platform made it unavailable.
Some aspects of the game, like Global Illumination Quality, Ray Traced Directional Shadows, and Texture Quality are already set to high on PlayStation 5 . The same aspects are sometimes lower or altogether absent on Xbox, though reports suggest the platforms have more parity than Sony's marketing would like you to believe.
There are even a couple of settings that Rockstar has already set to Ultra, such as Vehicle Max Texture Quality and Bounding Volume Hierarchy. A surprising number of settings — 18 to be exact — are set to medium or low on PS5 and Xbox Series X​​​​​​​ . That number jumps to 38 settings on Xbox Series X that are set to low or medium.​​​​​​​
The conservative presets are of significance for PC gamers. Settings such as Tree, Terrain, Impostor, and Grass Shadows are set to medium and affect draw distance and pop-in.​​​​​​​ Lighting and Ambient Lighting, which influence​​​​​​​ how the game renders background lights such as streetlights and neon signs, are also set to medium across platforms.
Image: Rockstar Games Volumetric Lighting​​​​​​​ , another setting currently on medium, determines how light is depicted in conditions such as fog and crepuscular rays​​​​​​​ . On consoles, aspects like 'god rays' can appear grainy or blocky — especially​​​​​​​ while the camera is in motion.
Even elements that might sound small on paper, like Weapon Textures, could meaningfully change the experience. There's a lot of shooting in this game, even if you play non-lethally; players will stare down the barrel of a gun for much of the game.
Players experiencing GTA 6 on PS5 Pro have slightly more presets set to high than the base platform​​​​​​​ , but by and large, a potential PC port​​​​​​​ of the game will likely look much better than its console counterparts, depending on hardware configuration. GTA 6 is no graphics slouch , either — so it's almost hard to fathom how this incredible-looking game is still nowhere near its full potential​​​​​​​ .

articles.t: GTA 6 Netflix Extended Look: 27 Minutes After Leaks
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 Netflix extended look: 27 minutes of PS5 footage, a six-hour exclusive window and unconfirmed CyberLeek leaks. What is confirmed and what is not.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games Netflix and Rockstar Games put Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look in front of subscribers on August 27, 2026, at 3 p.m. ET. It ran 27 minutes, and every frame came from in-game footage captured on PlayStation 5. For a franchise that has spent years rationing glimpses of its next entry, that is a lot of new material in one sitting.
The reveal did not arrive cleanly. Before the Netflix premiere, unauthorised videos claiming to show Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay spread across the internet, and Rockstar publicly called seeing that footage shared online “heartbreaking.” The tension between a carefully staged streaming event and a messy leak cycle is the real story here, and it says a lot about how big game launches now work.
This analysis walks through what is confirmed, what is not, and why the Netflix route matters for the publisher, the platforms and the people who just want to know what the game looks like. It also separates the claims made by a group calling itself CyberLeek (which remain unconfirmed, as we covered in our look at the CyberLeek executable leak ) from the facts Rockstar and Netflix have put on the record. For more game coverage, see our gaming section .
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Start with the hard facts, because the leak noise has blurred them. Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look is an official Netflix release. It is a collaboration between Netflix and Rockstar Games, and Rockstar’s parent publisher is Take-Two Interactive. Netflix says the presentation contains 27 minutes of new footage, and that all of it was captured in-game on PlayStation 5.
That last detail carries weight. A reveal built entirely from captured gameplay, rather than pre-rendered cinematics, tells viewers they are seeing something close to what players will actually run on a console. Rockstar and Netflix did not publish a technical breakdown of the capture, so we cannot say anything about resolution, frame rate or settings. Anyone quoting those numbers is guessing.
The game itself was scheduled for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19, 2026. No PC date is part of the confirmed record. Variety covered the Netflix trailer and Extended Look release when it went live. That November date has since passed, and our reporting on what followed sits in the linked coverage further down.
The release schedule is unusual enough to deserve its own section. Netflix premiered the presentation at 3 p.m. ET on August 27 and held exclusive access for six hours. Rockstar stated that the footage would then move to YouTube and other platforms at 9 p.m. ET. In other words, anyone without a Netflix account had to wait until the evening, while subscribers could press play in the afternoon.
Six hours is short by streaming-exclusive standards. It is long enough to give Netflix a real marketing hook, since the service could tell its audience that the biggest game reveal of the year started on its platform. It is short enough that Rockstar did not lock a huge portion of its audience out for days. Think of it as a head start rather than a wall.
Publishers usually announce games on their own channels or at industry showcases. Putting a GTA presentation on a streaming service is a different play, and Brandon Riegg, Netflix’s VP of nonfiction series, explained the appeal in a single line. He said: “Grand Theft Auto reveals have become cultural moments in their own right.”
Read that statement from Netflix’s side and the logic is clear. The service wants appointment viewing from audiences who might not watch a games showcase. A GTA presentation carries mainstream name recognition that few other entertainment properties can match, and Netflix gets to position itself as a home for event programming beyond scripted shows.
From Rockstar’s side, the benefits are less obvious but still real. A Netflix premiere brings its own promotional machine. It also lets the studio control the presentation format, length and sequencing in a way a livestreamed press event rarely allows. A single 27-minute piece is easier to polish than a live broadcast with commentary and ad breaks. Nothing in the confirmed record tells us the financial terms of the deal, and we will not guess at them.

Sauf que d'autres détails fuiteraient quand même du build : les réglages graphiques de chaque plateforme.
Ces informations non confirmées viennent du dataminer Text2. Elles tombent pile au moment où PlayStation affirme que GTA 6 tourne au mieux sur PS5. Quatre machines sont concernées : la PS5 Pro (nom de code Trinity), la PS5 (Prospero), la Xbox Series X (Anaconda) et la Xbox Series S (Lockhart).
Premier constat : la PS5 de base et la Xbox Series X utiliseraient des préréglages graphiques identiques, la Xbox Series S tournerait sur des réglages plus bas, et la PS5 Pro serait la seule plateforme avec des fonctions de ray tracing supplémentaires. Voilà ce qui ressort :
Un second tableau, bien plus fouillé, creuse davantage. Côté éclairage, la Global Illumination est en Medium sur Xbox Series S, Xbox Series X et PS5, et en High sur PS5 Pro.
Pour les ombres, les Directional Shadows sont en Medium sur Xbox Series S et en High sur Xbox Series X et PS5. Sur PS5 Pro, elles passent en Low avec le ray tracing actif. Même schéma pour les Local Shadows : Low sur Xbox Series S, High sur Xbox Series X et PS5, Low (RT actif) sur PS5 Pro.
La BVH Quality (RT Structure) est en Low sur Xbox Series S, High sur Xbox Series X et PS5, et Ultra sur PS5 Pro. Les RT Directional Shadows, RT Local Shadows et RT LOD Light Shadows sont désactivés (Off) sur Xbox Series S, Xbox Series X et PS5, et activés (High, High, true) sur PS5 Pro.
La Shadow Alpha Quality est en Low sur Xbox Series S, Medium sur Xbox Series X et PS5, et High sur PS5 Pro. Les Tinted Alpha Shadows sont désactivés (false) sur Xbox Series S et activés (true) sur les trois autres machines.
Les Texture Quality sont en Medium sur Xbox Series S et en High sur Xbox Series X, PS5 et PS5 Pro. La Tessellation est en Low sur Xbox Series S et en High ailleurs. La Hair Quality suit la même logique : Medium sur Xbox Series S, High sur les trois autres.
Une série de réglages place la Xbox Series S en Low et les trois autres en Medium : Grass Shadows, Terrain / Tree / Imposter Quality, Texture Streaming / Timecycle, Weapon Max Textures et Volumetrics Lighting. Seule exception, les Terrain Shadow Quality, en Medium partout.
Le Decoration Res Shift est de 1 sur Xbox Series S et de 0 sur les trois autres. Le Grass LOD / Manual Mip Bias est de 0.8 / -1.5 sur Xbox Series S et en Default ailleurs. La Hair GPU Budget / Simulation et la Particle Lighting sont en Low sur Xbox Series S et en High sur Xbox Series X, PS5 et PS5 Pro.
Le Motion Blur Scale est en Default (limite 16.0) sur Xbox Series S, Xbox Series X et PS5, et à 1.5 (limite 16.0) sur PS5 Pro. Le Vehicle Max Textures / HD Count est en Medium / 0 sur Xbox Series S, et en Ultra / 2 sur les trois autres.
Les Water Sim & Surface Waves sont en Medium sur Xbox Series S et en High sur Xbox Series X, PS5 et PS5 Pro. La Water Tessellation est en Low sur Xbox Series S et en Default sur les autres.
Enfin, les AI (Behavior, Motion, etc.), la Pedestrian & Vehicle Density et la Physics Quality sont en Medium sur Xbox Series S et en High sur Xbox Series X, PS5 et PS5 Pro.
Les visuels viseraient donc un niveau medium à high sur toutes les plateformes sauf la Xbox Series S. Un mode 60 FPS en baissant davantage les réglages reste difficile à dire. En revanche, en coupant aussi la résolution de rendu, un mode 45 FPS pourrait être atteignable, au prix de la qualité graphique. Ce n'est qu'une hypothèse.
Autre point curieux : la PS5 Pro ne proposerait pas de mode sans ray tracing, alors que son mode actuel est décrit à 30 FPS .

articles.t: Fuite de GTA 6 : la justice britannique prononce sept ans de prison - InfoMagazine Maroc
articles.chapeau: Le pirate à l’origine de la fuite de 90 vidéos de GTA 6 a été condamné le 23 novembre. Il avait aussi visé Revolut, Uber et BT/EE.
articles.txt:
Une peine de sept ans de prison, sans retour immédiat derrière les barreaux. Arion Kurtaj, 21 ans, a été condamné lundi 23 novembre à Londres pour plusieurs piratages commis en 2021 et 2022, dont celui de Rockstar Games à l’origine de la fuite de vidéos de GTA 6. Il a toutefois quitté le tribunal libre, compte tenu du temps déjà passé en détention, rapporte Le Parisien avec l’AFP.
Le jeune homme avait plaidé coupable le 16 novembre dans des affaires visant également Revolut, Uber et l’opérateur britannique BT/EE. Selon l’accusation, il appartenait au groupe de pirates informatiques Lapsus$.
L’intrusion chez Rockstar avait été menée en septembre 2022 depuis un hôtel de Bicester, près d’Oxford. Arion Kurtaj y avait été installé pour sa protection, après des menaces de pirates rivaux cherchant à s’emparer de bitcoins volés, selon la police de la City de Londres, chargée de l’enquête.
Depuis sa chambre, il avait utilisé un téléphone portable, la télévision connectée au wifi et une clé Amazon Fire Stick pour accéder aux systèmes du studio. Il avait ensuite dérobé et publié 90 vidéos de GTA 6 sous le pseudonyme « TeaPotUberHacker », plus d’un an avant la diffusion des premières images officielles. Le parquet britannique indique qu’il avait également menacé de rendre public le code source du jeu.
Ces faits intervenaient après une première arrestation. Entre août et novembre 2021, Kurtaj s’était introduit dans les systèmes de BT/EE avant de détourner de l’argent et des cryptomonnaies appartenant à des clients. Inculpé, il avait été remis en liberté sous caution.
Son parcours judiciaire a ensuite été marqué par une hospitalisation dans un établissement sécurisé. En 2023, il avait été déclaré inapte à suivre un procès classique en raison de son autisme. Jugé apte à plaider à l’été 2025, il avait été transféré en prison en janvier 2026.
Au moment de prononcer la peine, le juge Mark Turner, de la Woolwich Crown Court, a expliqué avoir tenu compte de la gravité des faits, mais aussi de l’âge de l’accusé lorsqu’il les avait commis et de ses antécédents médicaux. Il l’a averti de ne pas récidiver.

articles.t: GTA 6 sur PC : les moddeurs implorent les IA de « travailler plus vite » après la fuite d’une build Xbox
articles.txt:
La course pour faire tourner Grand Theft Auto 6 sur PC prend une tournure inédite. Après la fermeture du projet communautaire Project Leonida par Rockstar, d’autres groupes de moddeurs ont repris le flambeau, s’appuyant sur une prétendue build Xbox quasi finale du jeu ayant fuité cette semaine. Leur méthode : demander à des IA génératives de décompiler et recompiler le code, avec des prompts aussi directs que « travaille plus vite » ou « ne fais aucune erreur ».
Le point de départ de cette nouvelle vague d’activité est la diffusion, par le leaker connu sous le pseudonyme CyberLeek , d’une version du jeu décrite comme « quasi finale » pour Xbox . Cette build servirait de base aux travaux de portage vers PC. Auparavant, les communautés de moddeurs utilisaient déjà des outils d’IA pour analyser le code de la version console, mais cette fuite a démultiplié les tentatives.
Sur les réseaux sociaux, l’utilisateur chasm , qui suit de près ces communautés, a partagé des captures d’écran des invites envoyées aux chatbots. On y voit des moddeurs, parfois en direct sur des plateformes de streaming, demander à l’IA de « continuer à chercher des choses et à travailler », ou encore de « trouver un moyen plus rapide d’itérer ». Ces échanges illustrent une dépendance croissante à l’égard des modèles de langage pour mener à bien une tâche aussi complexe que le portage d’un jeu AAA.
Rockstar n’est pas resté inactif. Après avoir obtenu la suppression du serveur Discord et du dépôt GitHub de Project Leonida – y compris ses 3 006 forks – l’éditeur semble désormais cibler les publications en ligne qui documentent l’avancement de ces projets. L’utilisateur chasm a ainsi indiqué que ses propres messages avaient été retirés « en réponse à un signalement du détenteur des droits d’auteur ».
Cette stratégie de répétition des DMCA n’est pas nouvelle, mais elle prend ici une ampleur particulière en raison de la notoriété du jeu et de la détermination des moddeurs. La fermeture de Project Leonida n’a pas découragé les autres groupes, qui semblent au contraire redoubler d’efforts pour être les premiers à proposer une version jouable sur PC.
Une vidéo partagée sur les réseaux sociaux montre le jeu tournant sur PC, dépassant le simple écran de démarrage que les moddeurs avaient atteint quelques heures après la fuite. Les images, qui s’affichent à moins de 5 images par seconde , témoignent d’un rendu visuel correct mais d’une optimisation encore très loin des standards. Ce résultat, bien que préliminaire, prouve que la décompilation et la recompilation progressent.
Si Rockstar ne parvient pas à stopper ces initiatives, de nouvelles mises à jour sur l’avancement du portage pourraient voir le jour dans les prochains jours. La communauté reste très active, et les diffusions en direct des sessions de codage assisté par IA attirent un public curieux.
Pour l’instant, Grand Theft Auto 6 n’a été officiellement annoncé que sur PlayStation 5 et Xbox Series X/S , avec une sortie prévue à l’automne 2025. Rockstar n’a donné aucune indication sur une éventuelle version PC, ce qui alimente la frustration d’une partie des joueurs et explique l’empressement des moddeurs à créer leur propre portage.
Cette situation n’est pas sans rappeler les précédents de GTA V ou Red Dead Redemption 2 , dont les versions PC sont arrivées bien après les sorties console. Mais l’utilisation massive d’outils d’IA pour accélérer le processus est une nouveauté qui pourrait changer la donne, tant pour les moddeurs que pour les éditeurs.
En attendant une éventuelle annonce officielle, les joueurs PC devront se contenter de suivre de loin les avancées de ces projets non officiels, tout en gardant à l’esprit les risques juridiques encourus par leurs auteurs.

articles.t: GTA 6 Metacritic User Score: 5.6 vs 99 Critics
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 Metacritic user score sits near 5.6 while critics give a 99 Metascore from 152 reviews. Here is what the numbers and outlets confirm.
articles.txt:
Image: Rockstar Games Rockstar Games shipped Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19, 2026, and Metacritic now shows two very different verdicts. Critics gave it a 99 Metascore from 152 reviews, while the user score sits at 5.7 from 116,374 ratings . That works out to a 42-point gap once you put both numbers on the same 100-point scale.
The GTA 6 Metacritic user score has become the loudest argument in gaming this week. Some outlets call it review bombing. Others say players have real complaints and deserve a hearing. Our earlier piece on how GTA VI tied Ocarina of Time at 99 covered the critic side. This analysis covers the other half of the ledger, using only figures that named outlets reported and that Metacritic’s own listing confirms.
One caution before the details. The confirmed numbers show that the gap exists. They do not prove why it exists. No study, no Rockstar statement and no Metacritic announcement has established a single cause, so this article separates what the data shows from what outlets infer.
Google · Preferred Sources Don't miss new tech stories on Google
Add Shattered once in the Google app and our stories show up in your news suggestions.
Start with the critic side. Metacritic lists Grand Theft Auto VI, published by Rockstar Games, at a 99 Metascore built from 152 critic reviews. That score matches the all-time high that Nintendo’s Ocarina of Time has held for years. Yahoo’s entertainment desk, in a November 21 report by Marvin Montanaro , noted that IGN, GameSpot and Eurogamer all awarded perfect scores. Eurogamer’s own review called the game an open world of “awe, minute detail and impossible scale.”
Now the player side. Metacritic’s current listing shows a 5.7 user score from 116,374 ratings. On November 21, outlets reported 5.6 from 53,044 ratings. Eurogamer, writing the same day , described the figure as 5.6 out of 10 and said Metacritic classifies it as “mixed or average.” So the average climbed one tenth of a point while the sample more than doubled.
The 42-point gap is our arithmetic, not a figure Metacritic publishes. We multiplied the 5.7 user score by ten to match the critic scale. It gives readers a fast way to see how far apart the two groups sit.
The user score did not start at 5.6. Yahoo reported that earlier observations put the audience score in the 3 to 4 range before it began recovering. Eurogamer said the score “had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little.” Both outlets are describing the same pattern. Yahoo offered three possible reasons for the climb: genuine positive feedback, removal of suspicious ratings, or other shifts in who was rating.
That recovery matters for how you read any single screenshot. A score captured on launch night says little about the final picture. A score captured after 100,000 ratings says more, though even that remains a live average that shifts by the hour.
Between the November 21 snapshot and the current listing, the sample grew by 63,330 ratings. The score barely moved. That stability suggests the average has settled into a band rather than swinging wildly, which is useful for anyone trying to judge whether the early zeros were a spike or a trend.
It also means the large sample cuts against a pure “small group of trolls” explanation. A group of tens of thousands can still be coordinated, but the numbers alone cannot tell us that. The Tribune piece reported that 43 percent of ratings were negative at 101,402 ratings. A coordinated campaign would have to be very large to produce that share.
Critic scores behave differently from user scores. A reviewer gets a copy before launch, plays a defined portion or all of the game, and files a score under an editor’s eye. The 152 reviews behind the 99 Metascore came from outlets that put their names on the work. Eurogamer’s five-star review is one example, and Yahoo listed IGN and GameSpot as other perfect-score awards.
That process produces tight clusters. When 152 professional reviews average 99, almost every one of them sits at the top of the scale. The aggregator has little spread to work with, which is why a handful of lower scores would barely move the number, and why the score has stayed put.

articles.t: GTA 6 recompilers and vibe-coders implore AI chatbots to 'work faster' and 'make no mistakes' as they race to get the game running on PC
articles.chapeau: In the wake of Rockstar's takedown of the biggest community project working to make Grand Theft Auto 6 playable on PC, those remaining want to be the first to d
articles.txt:
Things continue to get messy in the community of players working on getting Grand Theft Auto 6 working on PC. The previous frontrunner, Project Leonida, got their Discord server and GitHub repository taken down by Rockstar , but others have seemingly stepped in to finish the job.
The most up-to-date build of GTA 6 was allegedly leaked earlier this week by notorious leaker CyberLeek . This is a supposedly near-final build of the game's Xbox version, and it's seemingly being used as the basis for the recent work to port the game to PC.
Unsurprisingly, most of these communities of modders rely almost exclusively on generative-AI tools like Claude and Antigravity to decompile and recompile the console version of GTA 6. That has always been the case, but the CyberLeek build only invited even more to ask AI chatbots to make the PC port for them.
X user chasm has been following developments in the GTA 6 decompile and recompile communities, and recently shared some of the prompts the so-called vibe-coders are using - a few of whom livestreamed the process.
"Make no mistakes," one modder prompted the AI chatbot. "Keep finding more stuff and working and pushing," another eloquently asked . "Work faster," asked another . "There has to be a faster way to iterate than this," they continued.
Rockstar, which successfully managed to DMCA take down Project Leonida - including all of its 3,006 forks on lead author NotRexed's GitHub - is seemingly also going after people online discussing the community's progress. The X user in question later revealed they may no longer be able to share these updates, as their posts have also been removed "in response to a report by the copyright owner" .
As for how far some of the remaining communities have managed to get, this video allegedly shows the game running on PC . This goes beyond the boot-up screen, which modders were able to reach within hours of CyberLeek's build alleged leaking .
The footage runs at sub-5fps, but the visuals look to have rendered normally. Assuming Rockstar doesn't also shut down the modders who remain active, we may see another progress update.
If you're already playing Rockstar's latest on consoles, the Eurogamer GTA 6 walkthrough offers comprehensive guides on relationship mechanics , how the new Criminal Profile system works , a list of all safe codes and more.

articles.t: Take-Two Appears to Be Trying to Scrub GTA 6 PC Ports From the Internet, as Vibecoders Race Toward Controversial World First
articles.chapeau: Take-Two appears to be taking on the many GTA 6 PC ports currently in the works following Cyberleek’s alleged release of an unauthorized Xbox build of the game.
articles.txt:
Take-Two appears to be taking on the many GTA 6 PC ports currently in the works following Cyberleek’s alleged release of an unauthorized Xbox build of the game.
This week, Cyberleek allegedly released the executable file for the incomplete GTA 6 Xbox build they reportedly leaked the week prior, sparking a race within the homebrew scene to port the build to PC. There’s even a website tracking the various attempts to recompile, emulate, or port the leaked Xbox Series build to PC.
But it looks like Take-Two is taking action, reportedly convincing GitHub to delete an entire network of 3,007 repositories via a DMCA takedown notice.
The takedown we know about relates to ItsNotRexed's GitHub repository and the over 2,900 forks attached to it, which Take-Two said facilitated copyright infringement of GTA 6. Take-Two alleged that the repository Project Leonida repository "exceeds the license Rockstar Games grants to users, constituting copyright infringement.” Here, Take-Two claimed that the repository violated at least Section 2.3 of Rockstar Games’ terms of service:
Additionally, there’s an interesting note in the takedown order that addresses the “bring your own files” defence we’ve seen so often from the homebrew community when it comes to unofficial ports of video games. As you’d expect, Take-Two isn’t in favor of it, insisting that in this case, the files the user must provide come from the unauthorized GTA 6 Xbox build Cyberleek leaked online.
According to now deleted social media posts, NotRexed, author of the Leonida project, shut it down entirely. There are also screenshots of its Discord showing users posting disclaimers distancing themselves from Project Leonida in case of a federal investigation.
However, many similar projects remain active, risking similar action from Take-Two. Seemingly undeterred, these projects are ongoing, with some getting close to creating a PC port of GTA 6 that is somewhat playable. Some are even streaming their efforts, showing how they are vibecoding a port using agent prompts such as "make no mistakes," "keep finding more stuff and working and pushing," and "work faster."
This is of course a nightmare scenario for Take-Two and Sony and Microsoft, which are benefiting greatly from GTA 6 releasing on console only. The console version of GTA 6 targets 30fps across all platforms, although struggles at times to hit that on base PS5, and Xbox Series X and S. As a result, there is huge interest in a potential PC version offering 60fps gameplay.
As you've probably seen from various viral clips on social media, people are using AI to create clones of popular games and release them on platforms they're not normally available on. We've seen everything from Minecraft playable inside X/Twitter to modders crashing Minecraft and Elden Ring together . Indeed, last month, Rockstar's own Grand Theft Auto 5 was made playable in a browser before it was pulled offline.
Seemingly in response, Anthropic issued an update for Claude that made it harder for people to use the AI model to generate video game clones. In an interview with IGN sister site RPS , former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij said that Rockstar Games may be keen to port GTA 6 to PC as soon as possible , due to the explosion of AI-generated clones and ports.
Some of this concern has to do with the security of the PS5, with Sony seemingly engaged in a game of Whac-a-Mole with hackers who are trying to jailbreak the latest firmware. If a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6 to run, it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and subsequently made available on PC.
Earlier this month, Strauss Zelnick, the boss of Take-Two, responded to the threat of AI-assisted reverse-engineering and decompilation of games in an interview with IGN. He said he was taking the issue seriously, and insisted that fans will prefer to play GTA 6 officially, with all its bells and whistles as Rockstar intended, over an unofficial PC version.
IGN: We've seen hackers using AI to clone games much faster than ever before, even try to jailbreak consoles. And there is some concern about this leading to potentially GTA 6 being made available on PC unofficially or places that you aren't releasing it. I was just wondering how much of a threat this is to your business? And, is there anything meaningful you can do about it?

articles.t: GTA 6 sur PC en mars 2027 : une fuite, aucune annonce
articles.chapeau: GTA 6 sur PC en mars 2027 avec GTA 6 Online ? Une fuite l’affirme sans preuve. Ce que Rockstar a dit, ce qui se contredit et ce qu’il faut savoir.
articles.txt:
GTA 6 sur PC en mars 2027, avec le lancement de son mode en ligne dans la foulée ? C’est ce qu’affirme une fuite partie d’un compte sur X, qui avance une date commune pour la version PC et pour un futur GTA 6 Online . Le problème, c’est que ni Rockstar ni Take-Two n’ont confirmé quoi que ce soit, et que la méthode décrite pour obtenir cette date n’est pas vérifiable. Nous avons donc recoupé l’information avec ce que les deux entreprises ont réellement dit.
Précisons le contexte. GTA 6 est sorti le 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S, et la page officielle du jeu ne mentionne toujours pas le PC. Les joueurs sur ordinateur attendent donc un signal, et c’est exactement ce qui rend ce genre de fuite aussi virale. Reste à savoir ce qu’elle vaut.
L’auteur du message explique avoir trouvé la date en analysant les documents financiers de Take-Two pour l’exercice 2027 avec un outil d’analyse, sans fournir la moindre preuve. Il affirme que Rockstar annoncerait le tout deux mois avant, et que le mode en ligne arriverait en mars 2027 sur PS5, Xbox Series X|S et PC. Le titre de la fuite parle d’une version PC du jeu principal, alors que le détail porte surtout sur le multijoueur.
Les chiffres cités pour donner du poids au message ne prouvent pas grand-chose. Les 8 milliards de dollars de prévision de chiffre d’affaires correspondent à la fourchette de 8,0 à 8,2 milliards déjà publiée par Take-Two, et les 9,69 millions de précommandes rappellent les estimations de tiers déjà connues pour les précommandes . Autrement dit, des données publiques ne valident pas une date inédite. Nous n’avons trouvé aucune confirmation indépendante de ce calendrier.
Le contenu décrit pour le mode en ligne reste à prendre avec les plus grandes précautions. Il comprendrait un personnage unique et permanent, des braquages en coopération, des courses de rue, des missions de contact, un système de gestion d’entreprise et des serveurs de jeu de rôle officiels conçus avec l’équipe de FiveM, que Rockstar a rachetée en 2023. Aucune progression ni aucun argent de GTA Online ne serait transféré. Rien de tout cela n’a été annoncé par Rockstar.
Du côté officiel, le silence domine. L’annonce de Rockstar du 10 novembre, consacrée au préchargement, présente les versions console, le jeu en streaming et le Remote Play, sans un mot sur le PC. Aucun nom, aucune date et aucun contenu n’ont non plus été annoncés pour un mode en ligne propre à GTA 6 au lendemain de la sortie.
Le patron de Take-Two, Strauss Zelnick, a expliqué en mai que Rockstar commence toujours par les consoles parce que le « cœur » du public s’y trouve, tout en reconnaissant que le PC représente désormais 45 à 50 % des ventes des grands titres du groupe. En septembre, il a laissé entendre que la plateforme devenait de plus en plus importante, sans date. Les rumeurs sur le calendrier, elles, se contredisent : un rapport appuyé sur quatre sources anonymes parlait déjà du premier trimestre 2027 pour le PC, d’autres signaux évoquaient un raccourcissement de la période d’exclusivité console , tandis que le mode en ligne était attendu un mois après le lancement, donc en décembre .
Une sortie avant le 31 mars 2027 aurait une logique comptable, puisque l’exercice fiscal de Take-Two se termine à cette date et que le groupe pourrait y inscrire les ventes PC. Le précédent historique plaide pourtant pour la prudence : GTA V avait attendu près de deux ans pour arriver sur PC, et Red Dead Redemption 2 plus d’un an. Un délai de quatre mois serait donc une rupture très nette avec les habitudes de Rockstar.
Mettre le PC et le mode en ligne dans le même panier relève, à ce stade, de l’hypothèse. Rien ne démontre que les deux sortiraient ensemble, et le fait que les rumeurs placent le mode en ligne en décembre, au début de 2027 ou en mars montre à quel point personne ne sait. Notez enfin que des projets amateurs tentent de lancer sous Windows la version Xbox du jeu apparue en ligne , sans qu’aucun build public vérifié ne prouve pour l’instant que le titre fonctionne. Le projet VIctory afficherait une première cinématique , ce qui reste très loin d’un jeu jouable.
Rockstar n’a communiqué aucune configuration, mais des estimations circulent déjà pour jouer en 60 FPS , à prendre comme un repère plutôt que comme un feu vert pour changer de carte. Sur console, le jeu tourne à 30 images par seconde et affiche un Metascore de 99 . Rien ne permet toutefois d’en déduire ce que serait une version PC.

articles.t: GTA 6 sur PC : Rockstar Games doit se dépêcher, la course pour créer une version non officielle a déjà commencé
articles.chapeau: Une fuite de la version Xbox de GTA 6 servirait de base pour des projets de recompilation du jeu vidéo pour PC.
articles.txt:
Depuis quelques jours, les joueurs sur PS5 et sur Xbox Series S ou X peuvent jouer à GTA 6. En revanche, ceux qui jouent sur PC doivent encore patienter, puisque le jeu n’est pas encore disponible sur cette plateforme et Rockstar Games n’a pas encore évoqué de date. Néanmoins, celui-ci aurait tout intérêt à accélérer le développement de la version PC de GTA 6 puisque sur internet, de nombreux projets pour créer un portage non officiel du jeu vidéo ont déjà été lancés. Selon les explications de PC Mag, tout a commencé par une fuite.
Vendredi, le hacker Cyberleek aurait posté une fuite de la version Xbox de GTA 6 , complétée par un exécutable clé partagé lundi. Ces fichiers ne permettent pas de jouer à GTA 6 sur PC (et ce serait du piratage), mais, comme la plateforme Xbox est proche du PC, ils pourraient servir de base pour créer un GTA 6 pour PC non officiel. Et, justement, le but de hacker était de passer le flambeau aux communautés open source.
Par ailleurs, certaines “communautés” commenceraient déjà à obtenir des résultats, en s’aidant de l’IA afin de faire de l’ingénierie inversée et de recompiler GTA 6 pour PC. Sur les réseaux sociaux, des vidéos montreraient que certains développeurs ont déjà réussi à démarrer le jeu sur PC, même si c’est pour le moment injouable.
Bien entendu, Rockstar Games ne reste pas les bras croisés face à ces tentatives de créer une version non officielle de GTA 6 sur PC. En effet, si quelqu’un réussissait à développer une expérience de jeu acceptable, cela plomberait les ventes de GTA 6 et surtout de la future version pour PC officielle. Sur X, une personne qui aurait déjà énormément avancé sur son projet de recompilation aurait annoncé abandonner, en partie parce que son serveur Discord a été fermé. Et, d’après le site Torrentfreak , à quelques heures du lancement de GTA 6, des projets de portage du jeu vidéo pour l’iPhone, le Mac et Android avaient déjà été fermés par GitHub.
Comme évoqué plus haut, on ne sait pas quand Rockstar lancera GTA 6 sur PC. Mais, selon les rumeurs, il est possible que cette version pour PC arrive dès le premier trimestre 2027. En attendant, il est préférable de ne pas cliquer si vous tombez sur un lien sur internet qui vous promet une version de GTA 6 sur PC.
En effet, des hackers essaient déjà de profiter de la frustration des joueurs sur PC pour piéger ceux-ci. Par exemple, dans un précédent article, nous avons évoqué un faux guide sous format PDF qui pousse les internautes à télécharger un malware. Et, d’après une publication de NordVPN , des kits d’arnaque pour piéger les internautes sont aussi commercialisés sur le dark web.
That’s what our Threat Intelligence team found on the dark web: a crypto wallet drainer, a fake “GTA6 Keygen.exe” that steals accounts, a YouTube Shorts bot to spread it, and a hidden crypto miner.

articles.t: Quelques heures après la dernière fuite de Cyberleek, les moddeurs ont déjà réussi à lancer GTA 6 sur PC et les progrès s
articles.chapeau: Quelques heures après la dernière fuite de Cyberleek, des moddeurs font déjà booter GTA 6 sur PC, écran titre et menus à l’appui. Mais derrière ces exploits spectaculaires, que vaut vraiment ce fameux « GTA 6 jouable sur PC » qui affole les réseaux ?
articles.txt:
Quelques heures après la dernière fuite de Cyberleek, des moddeurs font déjà booter GTA 6 sur PC, écran titre et menus à l’appui. Mais derrière ces exploits spectaculaires, que vaut vraiment ce fameux « GTA 6 jouable sur PC » qui affole les réseaux ?
Quelques heures après la mise en ligne du fichier exécutable Xbox de GTA 6 par le hacker Cyberleek , des moddeurs sont déjà parvenus à lancer le jeu sur PC. Sur certaines configurations, le logo de Rockstar Games apparaît, l’écran titre se charge, puis la séquence de configuration initiale défile comme sur console avant de planter. Pour un titre officiellement limité à la PS5 et à la Xbox Series, la vitesse des progrès surprend même les habitués de la scène modding.
Tout est parti de la fuite d’une build Xbox Series d’environ 209 Go, publiée le 19 novembre, mais inutilisable sur PC sans son exécutable. D’après Notebookcheck, ce dernier a été ajouté quelques jours plus tard, déclenchant une véritable course contre la montre pour faire booter GTA 6 nativement sous Windows. Où en est vraiment ce portage non officiel, et faut-il déjà croire aux vidéos de « GTA 6 jouable sur PC » qui envahissent les réseaux ?
La clé, c’est que la version Xbox Series de GTA 6 repose sur une architecture processeur x86-64, la même famille que la majorité des PC de jeu. Les kits de développement Xbox utilisent des API proches de DirectX 12, ce qui réduit la distance technique à parcourir pour Windows. Plutôt que d’émuler entièrement la console, les moddeurs peuvent réécrire une partie des appels système et traduire les shaders pour qu’ils soient acceptés par un GPU PC.
Résultat : alors qu’au départ le jeu se contentait de lancer l’exécutable avant de crasher immédiatement, Notebookcheck rapporte qu’il passe désormais l’écran de boot et tout l’outil de configuration initiale. Certaines équipes affirment même atteindre la cinématique d’intro autour de 30 à 40 images par seconde, mais aucun monde ouvert jouable et stable n’a été montré de façon crédible.
Un moddeur mentionne déjà environ 770 Go occupés sur SSD après décompression du dump Xbox et recompilation de plus de 26 000 shaders, ce qui donne une idée du chantier. À ce stade, l’expérience se limite à faire démarrer l’exécutable Xbox, afficher les menus et observer où le jeu plante pour corriger les appels manquants. Aucun installateur simple ni lanceur Windows « prêt à cliquer » n’existe pour le grand public.
Parallèlement, d’autres bidouilles ont consisté à faire tourner GTA 6 via une PS5 en streaming local sur PC, puis à injecter le DLSS 5 de Nvidia . Le DLSS est une technique qui rend le jeu dans une résolution plus basse puis reconstruit une image plus nette, ce qui permet de débloquer le frame rate au‑delà de 30 fps et d’améliorer la fluidité. Mais là encore, on reste dans le domaine de la démonstration technique, pas d’un port PC natif et distribué.
Notebookcheck estime qu’au rythme actuel, une build PC non officielle pourrait apparaître sur des sites de piratage dans les jours à venir. Cela ne signifie pas pour autant une version stable : la plupart de ces « GTA 6 PC full version » ont toutes les chances d’être des malwares déguisés , capables de voler mots de passe, comptes de jeu ou cryptomonnaies. Juridiquement, télécharger et exécuter ces fichiers reste de toute façon illégal.
Officiellement, Rockstar Games et Take-Two Interactive n’ont annoncé aucun port PC de GTA 6 . La seule façon légale d’y jouer sur ordinateur reste le Remote Play ou le cloud depuis sa propre console. Dans le même temps, l’auteur de la fuite se justifie : selon Notebookcheck, Cyberleek affirme « se battre contre les fonctionnalités verrouillées derrière des paywalls et les 20 dollars facturés en plus pour l’Ultimate Edition », tout en utilisant un memecoin $CYBERLEEK pour financer son projet, sans le rendre obligatoire pour accéder aux fichiers. Rockstar chercherait activement à l’identifier par des moyens juridiques, pour l’instant sans succès.
Au final, oui, GTA 6 boote déjà sur certains PC de moddeurs, ce qui est un signal fort sur la proximité technique entre Xbox Series et Windows. Mais non, il n’existe toujours pas de « GTA 6 jouable sur PC » accessible, fiable et sûr pour le joueur lambda. Pour l’instant, le feuilleton profite surtout aux passionnés de reverse engineering et aux cybercriminels à l’affût des plus impatients.

articles.txt:
조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 Rockstar Games' GTA Ⅵ(6) records approximately 5 trillion won in sales in just one day after its release. /Courtesy of Yonhap News Agency Hacked files from "Grand Theft Auto (GTA) 6," a crime action game considered this year's biggest hit, have been released, raising the likelihood that an unofficial PC version will emerge.
According to British gaming outlet Eurogamer on the 24th, Cyberleek, the anonymous hacker who breached Rockstar Games in August and leaked the game's entire development files, recently released the executable file for the Xbox version of GTA 6.
After leaking the full game build, Cyberleek had been receiving cryptocurrency donations while releasing stolen files and gameplay footage. Cyberleek had not released the executable (exe) file needed to run the game until making it public five days after the game's release.
A group of developers called "Project Leonida" downloaded the files released by Cyberleek and reportedly modified and ported the Xbox version to run on PCs with the help of the artificial intelligence (AI) tool Claude.
According to Eurogamer, one hacker reportedly managed to boot the game on a PC as far as the initial setup screen but failed to enter the game itself. They claim it will take about a week for the build to become playable on a PC.
GTA 6 was released worldwide on the 19th for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar Games typically releases games on consoles first and follows with a PC version about a year later.
But amid growing concern about the August hack and the prospect of an unofficial port using AI, some expect the company to bring forward the PC version's release to the first quarter of next year.

articles.t: Rockstar Games kills unauthorized 'GTA 6' PC port, for obvious reasons
articles.chapeau: Just wait for the official PC version of the game to come out.
articles.txt:
Don't try to port Grand Theft Auto VI to PC yourself — or you'll potentially find yourself in big legal trouble.
GTA 6 may finally be out on Xbox and PlayStation 5, but that doesn't help out the PC gaming faithful, who still have much longer to wait for their version of the game.
As a result, some impatient gamers have recently attempted to create PC ports of the game themselves. Notorious GTA 6 leaker, Cyberleek, also recently released an executable .exe file of the Xbox build of the game, which helped those efforts. Even without Cyberleek, these efforts were probably inevitable, as new AI tools have led to a surge in PS5 jailbreaks and unauthorized ports of classic video games.
However, Rockstar Games' parent company, Take-Two Interactive, clearly does not approve of these unofficial attempts to bring GTA 6 to PC ahead of schedule. On Monday, the company had the biggest GTA 6 PC port project, known as Leonida, taken down. So far, GTA 6 has generated billions of dollars, and the PC version could bring in billions more. And when it comes to protecting their IP, Take-Two and Rockstar aren't messing around.
GitHub, where the project was hosted, posted a Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) notice it received from Take-Two.
"We are the IP Enforcement Team for Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., parent company of Rockstar Games," the notice reads. "We are writing to submit a takedown request regarding ItsNotRexed's GitHub repository and the 2900+ forks attached to it that infringes upon Take-Two's copyrighted works and facilitates copyright infringement of Rockstar Games title, Grand Theft Auto VI."

"On November 20, 2026, stolen game files from an Xbox Series build of Grand Theft Auto VI were publicly distributed," the takedown notice reads. "The following day, this Leonida repository opened with the purpose of running the Xbox Series version of GTA VI on PC. Its README requires Xbox Series game files as input."
According to Take-Two, Leonida attempts to get around the IP issues by instructing project contributors to "bring your own files."
"This is intentionally misleading," Take-Two explains, pointing out that the files in question are the unauthorized GTA 6 files leaked by Cyberleek.
As our colleagues at PCMag point out , this is just one of many unauthorized projects attempting to bring GTA 6 to PC before the official version comes out. (Disclosure: Mashable and PCMag are both owned by the same parent company, Ziff Davis.) Other projects have reportedly managed to get the game's opening scene running on PC. Another has an extremely degraded version of the game running on Mac.
According to the Leonida project admin , Take-Two also successfully had the Discord server for the GTA 6 porting project taken down as well, so it does seem like the company is going to ramp up its takedowns of any attempted GTA 6 ports.
GTA 6 for PC has no official release date. However, GameBeat recently reported that the PC version may be released in early 2027, well before most gamers expected.
